title: Policy engine guardrails for safe fallback/degradation policies (prevent loops, unsafe cross-tier/cross-region)
creator: Jordan Lee
body:
## Context
As part of Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (ENG-4821), we’re adding customer-configurable fallback/degradation policies (e.g., fallback model variant, region, capacity tier where applicable) so the platform can degrade gracefully instead of timing out.

We need *policy-level guardrails* so customers (and internal defaults) cannot configure unsafe policies that:
- create infinite fallback loops (A -> B -> A)
- cause runaway request amplification (multi-hop fallback chains under overload)
- violate tier isolation (e.g., accidentally “fallback” into higher-cost paths)
- cause cross-region thrash/ping-pong that increases tail latency and load
- produce ambiguous client behavior (e.g., repeated retryable errors without clear guidance)

This ticket focuses on the policy engine validation and runtime safety checks. It does **not** replace quotas/rate limits.

## Problem statement
Fallback is helpful during partial brownouts, but unsafe configuration can create a *cascading failure amplifier*: the platform keeps re-routing the same work, increasing load and tail latency during exactly the conditions we’re trying to protect against.

We want deterministic, bounded behavior:
- at config time: reject unsafe policies with clear error messages
- at runtime: enforce hard caps/guards even if a bad config slips through (or in case of legacy configs)

## Goals
1) Prevent infinite or long fallback chains by enforcing:
- acyclic fallback graph
- max fallback depth / hop count
- no self-referential fallbacks

2) Prevent unsafe “tier escalation” / “cost escalation” fallbacks:
- default: only allow same tier or explicit downgrade (Hosted tier semantics)
- never allow fallback that increases per-token cost profile by default (unless explicitly allowed by internal allowlist)

3) Reduce cross-region thrash:
- default: allow at most one cross-region hop
- forbid multi-region cycles
- enforce region allowlist (customer can only fallback into enabled regions)

4) Make failure behavior predictable:
- when fallback policy is blocked/invalid at runtime, return standardized overload error with a reason indicating policy rejected/guardrail triggered (must align with overload error taxonomy)

## Non-goals
- Designing the entire fallback feature surface area (handled in the routing/control plane tickets + PRD)
- Dedicated-specific SLA semantics (tracked in ENG-4837; we only implement generic guardrails and feature gating here)

## Proposed guardrails (initial)
### A) Static validation (on policy create/update)
**Validation checks** (reject with actionable message):
- Acyclic: construct directed graph of fallbacks between (model, region, tier) targets and ensure no cycles.
- Depth: enforce `max_hops <= 2` by default (configurable by Redwood, not customer-editable initially).
- Self-loop: forbid fallback target identical to source.
- Region allowlist: fallback region must be in customer’s enabled/contracted regions.
- Model compatibility: fallback model must be in same compatibility family (tokenization + endpoint type). If unknown, require explicit “allow_unsafe_model_fallback” flag (internal only).
- Tier constraints (Hosted): forbid any fallback that implies higher priority/cost tier than the request’s tier.

### B) Runtime enforcement
Even with validated policies, runtime needs a hard cap:
- Attach a `fallback_hops_remaining` counter to request context (initialized from server-side default).
- Enforce monotonic decrement on each fallback attempt.
- If exhausted, stop attempting fallbacks and return standardized overload response (don’t silently retry).
- Ensure we cannot bounce between regions/services due to partial signal flaps.

### C) Observability
Emit counters and traces for:
- policy_validation_rejected_total{reason}
- fallback_guardrail_triggered_total{reason}
- fallback_attempt_total{from,to,reason} (labels must be bounded; see cardinality guidance from observability review)

## Product/compat notes
- Error surface must align with overload error mapping (ADR-0147) and include deterministic “do/don’t retry” semantics.
- SDK teams (ENG-4836) need to be able to classify “guardrail blocked” separately from capacity overload.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Policy engine rejects cycle configs with a clear message that identifies the cycle path.
- [ ] Policy engine rejects fallback depth > server default.
- [ ] Policy engine rejects cross-region fallback to non-enabled region.
- [ ] Policy engine rejects tier escalation (Hosted) unless internal allowlist is used.
- [ ] Runtime hop counter prevents more than N fallbacks even if routing retries.
- [ ] Metrics/traces exist for (a) rejected configs and (b) runtime guardrail triggers.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: self-loop, simple cycle, multi-node cycle, max depth, cross-region constraints.

## References
- Drive: circuit-breaker config schema draft (policy/fallback section): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/circuit-breaker-config-schema-draft.json
- PRD: Hosted overload protection customer experience: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-hosted-overload-protection-customer-experience.json
- ADRs: error taxonomy + mapping (ADR-0147), breaker hysteresis model (ADR-0148)

## Open questions
1) What is the default `max_hops` we want for Hosted? Proposal: 1 hop for cross-region, 2 hops total.
2) Do we allow fallback to a “cheaper” model variant automatically (e.g., quantized) if customer opted in? If yes, how do we represent “quality tiers” in policy safely?
3) How do we gate enterprise exceptions (support-managed allowlist vs contract metadata)?

## Implementation plan
- Add validation module in policy engine service (config write path).
- Add request context field for hop tracking and wire into routing evaluation.
- Add structured reason codes for guardrail triggers (coordinate with error taxonomy ticket).
- Add metrics + minimal dashboard panels (handoff to ENG-4829/ENG-4830).
comments: 2025-11-18 (Jordan Lee): Kicked off design with Mina/Ravi. We’re seeing early configs from prospects that try to specify fallback chains across multiple regions/models. We need to treat fallback as a *bounded DAG* and enforce hard hop limits server-side (not customer-controlled initially).

2025-11-21 (Rafael Mendes): +1 on runtime hop counter. We should assume “bad configs” happen and also that signals can flap. Suggest adding a cool-down per request for region change (even 1 hop) to prevent ping-pong if breaker flips half-open quickly.

2025-11-27 (Henry Cho): From a customer-experience standpoint we need clear messaging when config is rejected. Please include exact field path + what’s allowed (e.g., “fallback.region must be one of [us-east-1, eu-west-1]”). Also confirm what error code we’ll return if runtime guardrail triggers.

2025-12-02 (Benji Okafor): We should implement most of this as schema validation + a graph validation pass. I can help wire it into the existing config rollout primitives. Note: we need an internal override mechanism for enterprise support (maybe a per-account capability flag).

2025-12-09 (Jordan Lee): Drafted validation rules. Biggest debate: allowing fallback to different model families. Proposal is to forbid by default unless both are in the same “compat family” (tokenizer + endpoint type), and even then limit to curated Redwood variants. Will sync with Brian (error semantics) re: guardrail-triggered error mapping.
2026-01-06 (Jordan Lee): Implemented cycle detection + max depth checks locally; adding tests next. Runtime hop counter implementation depends on routing request context plumbing (ENG-4824/ENG-4825).

2026-01-22 (Lauren Bishop): Please ensure Dedicated behavior is feature-gated. Dedicated customers may have different expectations (e.g., prefer queueing over fallback). Let’s default these guardrails off for Dedicated until ENG-4837 lands with agreed semantics.
